summary: Serverless-first design: React Native (Expo) + Next.js, Supabase (BaaS), Supabase Postgres database on Cloudflare Pages. It matches the team's languages and is estimated at $130-$340 per month.

frontend.justification: React Native (Expo) + Next.js matches the team's typescript/javascript skills; Next.js serves the web and React Native (Expo) the mobile app, so each platform gets a first-class client; renders pages ahead of time or on the server, which search engines can index; JavaScript team, OTA updates, managed builds.

alternatives.why_not: Flutter + Next.js scores 0.7 points lower overall, mainly on team skill fit (0.4 points).
Kotlin + Jetpack Compose (Android native) + Next.js scores 0.9 points lower overall, mainly on team skill fit (0.5 points).

tradeoffs: Two client codebases to build and maintain.

backend.justification: Supabase (BaaS) matches the team's typescript/javascript skills; is a managed backend, so there are no servers to run; handles many concurrent realtime connections well; Auth, REST/GraphQL, storage, realtime out of the box.

alternatives.why_not: Python + Django scores 2.7 points lower overall, mainly on budget fit (2.6 points) and compatibility with the rest of the stack (0.9 points). Estimated infrastructure about $260-$520/month versus about $130-$320/month.
Next.js route handlers (serverless) scores 3.6 points lower overall, mainly on time to market (1.0 points) and budget fit (0.9 points).

database.justification: Supabase Postgres gives ACID transactions for money-handling data; can be placed in Mumbai (ap-south-1) to keep data in India; has headroom for the expected load; dashboard, auth and APIs on top.

alternatives.why_not: PostgreSQL (managed or self-hosted) scores 2.8 points lower overall, mainly on budget fit (3.6 points) and performance (0.9 points). Estimated infrastructure about $350-$640/month versus about $130-$320/month.

MySQL (managed or self-hosted) scores 4.0 points lower overall, mainly on budget fit (3.6 points) and performance (0.9 points). Estimated infrastructure about $350-$640/month versus about $130-$320/month.

tradeoffs: Paid plan needed for production SLAs

hosting.justification: Cloudflare Pages has no contractual SLA, though about 99.9% uptime is typical; accept that for the 99.9% target or choose a host with an SLA; git deploys, previews.

alternatives.why_not: Firebase Hosting scores 2.1 points lower overall, mainly on budget fit (1.1 points) and performance (0.4 points). Estimated infrastructure about $130-$450/month versus about $130-$320/month.
Azure Static Web Apps scores 2.5 points lower overall, mainly on budget fit (0.9 points) and time to market (0.5 points). Estimated infrastructure about $130-$440/month versus about $130-$320/month.

tradeoffs: No published uptime SLA below the Enterprise plan
Upper cost estimate ($130-$320/month) exceeds the $150 budget at peak.

assumptions: Load estimate: peak about 80 requests/second and about 20M requests/month from 30K users in 12 months.
Usage-priced items are shown as a band (0.75x to 1.3x of the estimate) because load figures are order-of-magnitude.
Public list prices of each product, in USD, without taxes, committed-use discounts or developer time.
The 99.9% availability target doubles or adds redundancy for hosting and database where needed.
Observability (UptimeRobot / Better Stack uptime checks): about $0-$6/month

warnings.message: Estimated build effort is about 24 person-weeks against roughly 16 available in 8 weeks; reduce scope, drop a platform, or lean on managed services.
Use a hosted checkout from a PCI DSS certified provider so card data never reaches your servers.
SMS to Indian numbers needs DLT registration (entity, sender ID and message templates) with a telecom operator before launch; allow one to two weeks.
DPDP Act: record consent, support erasure and correction, notify breaches, and take extra care with children's data. Cross-border transfer is allowed except to countries the government restricts.

Expected cost ($130-$340) has its midpoint above the $150 budget; the low end fits. The largest items are database (Supabase Postgres, $79-$190) and SMS (MSG91, $55-$120), so start there: trim optional services, cap usage, or accept a tighter margin.
Razorpay: use Standard Checkout or hosted fields so card numbers are tokenised by Razorpay and never touch your servers; this keeps you in the lightest PCI DSS scope.
SMS one-time passwords through MSG91 cost about $55-$120 per month, a large share of the budget; email magic links, passkeys or WhatsApp OTP cut this, and SMS can stay as a fallback.

A heavier setup (Python + Django with PostgreSQL (managed or self-hosted) on Fly.io) was considered and is 2.9 points behind; 1.6 of those points come from the extra complexity and operations work it puts on a team of 3 without a DevOps engineer.

assumptions: No extra inputs supplied; neutral defaults are used (learning appetite medium, lock-in tolerance medium, budget strictness firm, no hiring plan, no mobile preference).
No compatible stack fits the $150 budget, so cost was compared against a reference of about $320 per month (the cheapest compatible stack plus 25%) to keep the cheaper options ahead.
No cache layer: about 80 requests/second and 30,000 users in 12 months are served directly by the database or BaaS.
No queue: background work is light enough for the backend or the provider's own webhooks and functions.

pipeline: filter each layer by hard constraints
